findings.message: The yaml-language-server schema header is written inside a double-quoted PowerShell string, so PowerShell expands `$schema` as an undefined variable. Every generated manifest gets the broken header `# yaml-language-server: =https://...` instead of the schema reference the change says the winget-pkgs pipeline requires. Lines 209, 222 and 243 are `@("# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://aka.ms/winget-manifest.version.1.12.0.schema.json", ...` in a `shell: pwsh` step. In an expandable (double-quoted) string `$schema` is a variable reference that ends at `=`, and nothing assigns `$schema`. The text therefore never contains `$schema=`. The comment at lines 201-204 says the pipeline 'fails manifest validation' without this header, so every 'Submit to winget' run still uploads manifests that fail. A single-quoted string or an escaped `` `$schema `` is needed.

The publish triggers were narrowed to source-file extensions and no longer list the workflow file itself. A merged PR that changes only a version, dependency, font, manifest or workflow file now publishes nothing, and nothing in the story asked for this. In the diff, `FIGLet.Python/**` became `FIGLet.Python/**/*.py`. Likewise `FIGLet/**` became `FIGLet/**/*.cs`, `FIGLet.TS/**` became `*.ts`/`*.tsx` only, `FIGPrint/**` became `*.cs`, and the VS and VS Code extension paths changed the same way. Every `.github/workflows/publish-*.yml` self-path was removed. publish-figlet-py.yml line 38 reads the major.minor base version from `pyproject.toml`, so a merged PR that only bumps it (or changes `fonts/small.flf`) no longer runs the publish job. The same goes for `FIGLet.TS/package.json`, `*.csproj`, `.vsixmanifest`/`.xaml` and the extension's `package.json`. Changes to the workflow files themselves, including this one's fixes to publish-figprint.yml, also wait for an unrelated `.cs` change to run. The only fallback is a manual `workflow_dispatch`.

insertBanner no longer replaces a non-empty selection: it always inserts at column 0 of the cursor's line. Selected text the user expected to be replaced stays in the document, and this behaviour change is undocumented and was not requested. The diff removes `if (editor.selection.isEmpty) { editBuilder.insert(...) } else { editBuilder.replace(editor.selection, ...) }` and keeps only `editBuilder.insert(position, indentedBanner + '\n')`, where `position = currentPosition.with(currentPosition.line, 0)` and `currentPosition = editor.selection.active` (the selection's active end). None of the ChangeLog-2026.md entries in the diff mention this change.

The rewritten installer manifest drops `PortableCommandAlias: figprint`, but the new changelog entry says it defines `figprint` as the portable command alias. The changelog now describes a manifest the workflow doesn't produce. The removed manifest had `"  PortableCommandAlias: figprint",`. The new NestedInstallerFiles entries (lines 253-254 and 261-262) list only `- RelativeFilePath: FIGPrint.exe`. ChangeLog-2026.md says: 'Define `FIGPrint.exe` as the nested installer file with `figprint` as the portable command alias'.

A user's existing `figlet.defaultFont` value is silently ignored after upgrade, because the new last-used-font lookup falls back to 'small' rather than migrating the old setting. `const lastFontUsed = context.globalState.get<string>('lastFontUsed') || 'small';`. The `figlet.defaultFont` contribution is removed from package.json, and no code reads the old value as a fallback.

The new enum member is named `BATCHFile`, which matches neither the PascalCase of the other members nor the `BatchFile` name the changelog says was introduced. The enum adds `BATCHFile` next to `Bash` and the others. The static property is `LanguageCommentStyles.BatchFile = new CommentStyleInfo(CommentStyle.BATCHFile)`. ChangeLog-2026.md says 'Introduce `BatchFile` to `CommentStyle` enum'.

`$PackageId` is assigned a second time, which duplicates the earlier `$packageId`. PowerShell variable names are case-insensitive, so both names refer to one variable, and the two spellings in the same step mislead the reader. Line 152 has `$packageId  = "ByteForge.FIGPrint"` and line 193 has `$PackageId = "ByteForge.FIGPrint"`. Both spellings are then used: `$PackageId` in the manifests, `$packageId` in the upload message and PR title.

Inserting a banner with text selected no longer replaces the selection, leaving the original text in the document. The previous nonempty-selection branch called editBuilder.replace(editor.selection, ...); insertBanner now always calls editBuilder.insert at column zero of the selection's active line. Selecting an existing banner and generating its replacement therefore retains the old banner and adds another.

The generated schema directives lose the literal $schema key, so the added schema references do not work. All three header strings use PowerShell double quotes, for example "# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://aka.ms/winget-manifest.version.1.12.0.schema.json". The script never assigns $schema, so interpolation produces '# yaml-language-server: =https://...' before Set-Content writes and uploads the manifests.

The narrowed publishing filters skip releases for changes to packaged resources and build metadata. The FIGPrint trigger now matches only FIGPrint/**/*.cs, although FIGPrint.csproj embeds fonts/small.flf and configures other font assets. A merged PR fixing only those fonts or the project file no longer starts publishing. The same narrowing across the other publishing workflows excludes their non-source package inputs, and workflow_dispatch is the only remaining fallback.
